prompt: The most important aim of science should be to improve people’s lives. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement? Give reasons for your answer and include relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.
essay:
Science has played a fundamental role in human development, from improving healthcare to creating technologies that make everyday activities easier. I strongly agree that improving people’s lives should be the primary aim of scientific progress, although scientific research can also serve other purposes.

One major reason for prioritising human well-being is that scientific discoveries can directly improve people’s health and life expectancy. Advances in medicine have led to vaccines, antibiotics and sophisticated treatments for diseases that were once life-threatening. For example, the development of vaccines has helped prevent millions of people from suffering from infectious diseases. Similarly, modern medical technology allows doctors to diagnose illnesses at an earlier stage and provide more effective treatment. Therefore, scientific research can have a profound impact on both the length and quality of human life.

In addition, science has contributed greatly to improving people's daily lives through technological and engineering developments. Modern transportation, electricity, the internet and household appliances have made many tasks faster, safer and more convenient. For instance, advances in engineering have resulted in elevators and hydraulic systems that allow people to move heavy objects with considerably less physical effort. Furthermore, scientific research into renewable energy could help societies reduce pollution and address the long-term threat of climate change. These examples demonstrate that science can be used not only to make life more convenient but also to solve major problems facing humanity.

However, not every scientific discovery has an immediate or obvious benefit to human life. Some research is conducted simply to expand our understanding of the natural world. For example, research into distant galaxies or subatomic particles may not produce an immediate practical application. Nevertheless, such research can eventually lead to unexpected technological breakthroughs and a deeper understanding of our environment. Therefore, even scientific research that appears unrelated to everyday life can ultimately contribute to human progress.

In conclusion, I strongly agree that improving human life should be the most important aim of science. Although expanding knowledge is also valuable in its own right, scientific research is most beneficial when its discoveries can contribute to better health, greater convenience and a safer and more sustainable future.
